architect.node.bubble.twitch_charitydona: Fires when a viewer donates to the channel's active Twitch charity campaign. User is the donor, Amount is the donated value with its cents intact, Currency is the ISO code and CharityName is the beneficiary. Amount rides the canonical money path, so it keeps its decimals.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_charitystar: Fires when a Twitch charity campaign opens on the channel. CharityName is the beneficiary, Amount is the total raised so far, TargetAmount is the campaign goal and Currency is the ISO code. Amount and TargetAmount keep their cents — they ride the canonical money path.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_charityprog: Fires whenever the running total of the active Twitch charity campaign moves. CharityName is the beneficiary, Amount is the new total raised, TargetAmount is the goal and Currency is the ISO code. Amount keeps its cents.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_charitycomp: Fires when a Twitch charity campaign ends. CharityName is the beneficiary, Amount is the final total raised, TargetAmount is the goal that was set and Currency is the ISO code. Compare Amount against TargetAmount to tell a met goal from a missed one; both keep their cents.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_goalbegin: Fires when the broadcaster starts a channel goal. GoalId identifies the goal and GoalType is Twitch's own type string (follow, subscription, new_bit, new_cheerer and so on). Description is the label shown to viewers; CurrentAmount is the count the goal opens at and TargetAmount is what it aims for.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_goalprogres: Fires each time a channel goal moves. CurrentAmount is the new count and TargetAmount is the target; GoalId identifies which goal moved, GoalType is Twitch's own type string (follow, subscription, new_bit, new_cheerer and so on) and Description is the viewer-facing label.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_goalend: Fires when a channel goal closes. IsAchieved is true when the target was reached and false when the broadcaster ended it short. CurrentAmount is the final count against TargetAmount; GoalId, GoalType (follow, subscription, new_bit, new_cheerer and so on) and Description identify the goal.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_shoutoutcre: Fires when you shout another channel out — the outgoing direction. TargetUser is the channel you promoted and ViewerCount is how many of your viewers saw the shoutout. Use Twitch.ShoutoutReceived for shoutouts pointed at you.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_shoutoutrec: Fires when another broadcaster shouts your channel out — the incoming direction. User is the channel that promoted you and ViewerCount is how many of their viewers saw it. Use Twitch.ShoutoutCreated for shoutouts you send.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_userbanned: Fires when a viewer is permanently banned from the channel. User is the banned viewer, Moderator is who issued it and Reason is the optional note from the moderation log. Twitch itself sends bans and timeouts as one event; Streamer.bot splits them, so this node covers permanent bans only.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_usertimedou: Fires when a viewer is timed out. User is the timed-out viewer, Moderator is who issued it, Reason is the optional note and Duration is the timeout length in seconds. Twitch sends bans and timeouts as one event; Streamer.bot splits them, so permanent bans arrive on Twitch.UserBanned instead.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_userunbanne: Fires when a permanent ban is lifted. User is the viewer who got their access back and Moderator is who lifted it. Streamer.bot splits Twitch's combined unban event, so a timeout cleared early arrives on Twitch.UserUntimedOut instead.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_useruntimed: Fires when an active timeout is cleared before it expires. User is the viewer who got their access back and Moderator is who cleared it. Streamer.bot splits Twitch's combined unban event, so a lifted permanent ban arrives on Twitch.UserUnbanned instead.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_watchstreak: Fires when a viewer hits a watch streak. Streak is how many consecutive broadcasts they have shown up for, User is the viewer, PointsAwarded is the channel points Twitch handed out for the streak and Message is the chat line carrying the streak notice.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_announcemen: Fires when the broadcaster or a moderator posts a channel announcement. User is who posted it, Message is the announcement text and Color is the highlight colour Twitch rendered it with — DEFAULT, BLUE, RED, ORANGE or PURPLE.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_automaticre: Fires when a viewer redeems one of Twitch's built-in channel-point rewards, such as Highlight My Message. RewardType names which built-in reward fired, ChannelPoints is what it cost, User is the redeemer and Message is any text they attached. Custom rewards you created yourself arrive on Twitch.PointRedeem instead.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_pollcreated: Fires when a poll opens on the channel. Title is the poll question and PollId identifies it, so a later Twitch.PollCompleted can be matched back to this one.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_pollupdated: Fires each time votes come in on the running poll. Title is the poll question and PollId identifies which poll moved.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_pollcomplet: Fires when a poll closes. Title is the poll question and PollId identifies it. Pair with Twitch.PollCreated to bracket a poll from open to close.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_predictionc: Fires when a channel-points prediction opens. Title is the prediction question and PredictionId identifies it. WinningOutcome is empty here — nothing has been resolved yet.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_predictionu: Fires each time viewers commit more channel points to the running prediction. Title is the prediction question and PredictionId identifies it; WinningOutcome stays empty until the prediction is resolved.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_predictionl: Fires when the prediction window closes and no more points can be committed. Title and PredictionId identify the prediction; WinningOutcome is still empty because the broadcaster has not picked a winner yet.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_predictionc: Fires when the broadcaster resolves a prediction and pays it out. WinningOutcome names the outcome that won — this is the only prediction node where that socket carries a value. Title and PredictionId identify the prediction.
Fires when a prediction is cancelled and every committed point is refunded. Title and PredictionId identify it; WinningOutcome stays empty because nothing won.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_chatcleared: Fires when the whole chat history is wiped by a moderator or the broadcaster. There is no per-message detail — Twitch reports the clear as a single channel-wide event.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_moderatorad: Fires when someone is granted moderator status on the channel. User is the new moderator.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_moderatorre: Fires when moderator status is taken away. User is the viewer who lost it.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_vipadded: Fires when someone is granted VIP status on the channel. User is the new VIP.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_vipremoved: Fires when VIP status is taken away. User is the viewer who lost it.
architect.node.bubble.value_bool: Outputs a fixed boolean (true or false). Edit Value inline on the node body. Wire the Input socket to override the inline value at runtime (a wired value always wins). Pure data — no flow pin.
architect.node.bubble.value_float: Outputs a fixed decimal number. Edit Value inline on the node body. Wire the Input socket to override the inline value at runtime (a wired value always wins). Pure data — no flow pin.
architect.node.bubble.value_int: Outputs a fixed whole number. Edit Value inline on the node body. Wire the Input socket to override the inline value at runtime (a wired value always wins). Pure data — no flow pin.
architect.node.bubble.value_string: Outputs a fixed string. Edit Value inline on the node body. Wire the Input socket to override the inline value at runtime (a wired value always wins). Pure data — no flow pin.
architect.node.bubble.var_get: Reads a local script variable named {var.<VariableName>}. Edit VariableName inline on the node. Pure data — no flow pin. Branch-local: a value written inside an Async.Parallel branch does NOT leak back to the parent script. Use Public.Get when a branch needs to share the value, or DB.GetVariable for values that survive the script run.
architect.node.bubble.var_set: Writes Value into a local script variable named {var.<VariableName>}. Edit VariableName inline on the node. Branch-local: writes inside an Async.Parallel branch do NOT merge back to the parent — they vanish when the branch ends. Use Public.Set when a branch needs to share the value with the rest of the script, or DB.SetVariable for values that survive the script run.
architect.node.bubble.visual_trigger: Fires a Visualist widget's named trigger and continues immediately — does not wait for the overlay to finish. Use Async.WaitForVisual when you need to wait. LayerID is the .phxlayer filename stem (no extension); WidgetID is the widget's GUID; TriggerName is e.g. "onTrigger:greet". Wire a list (Array.Make / Array.Literal) into Args to deliver positional values; widget-side nodes reference them as {Args1}, {Args2}, {ArgsN} in Text.Render and as the When attribute on Result.If. Wire values into the dynamic input sockets — each socket's name becomes a key in the trigger's EventData on the widget side.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_ban: Permanently hides User from your YouTube live chat. There is no unban from inside Phoenix — lift the ban in YouTube Studio.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_betterttve: Fires when a BetterTTV emote is added to the channel's YouTube emote set. EmoteName is the emote; Payload carries the raw event JSON.
Fires when a BetterTTV emote is removed from the channel's YouTube emote set. EmoteName is the emote; Payload carries the raw event JSON.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_broadcasta: Fires when a new broadcast is created or scheduled on the YouTube channel. Title, BroadcastId, Privacy, and Status describe the new broadcast.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_broadcaste: Fires when a YouTube broadcast ends. Title, BroadcastId, Privacy, and Status describe the broadcast that just finished.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_broadcastm: Fires when Streamer.bot stops monitoring a YouTube broadcast. Title and BroadcastId identify the broadcast; Payload carries the raw event JSON.
Fires when Streamer.bot starts monitoring a YouTube broadcast. Title and BroadcastId identify the broadcast; Payload carries the raw event JSON.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_broadcastr: Fires when a broadcast is removed from the YouTube channel. Title, BroadcastId, Privacy, and Status describe the removed broadcast.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_broadcasts: Fires when a YouTube broadcast goes live. Title, BroadcastId, Privacy, and Status describe the broadcast that just started.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_broadcastu: Fires when a broadcast's metadata changes on the YouTube channel. Title, BroadcastId, Privacy, and Status carry the updated values.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_createpoll: Creates a poll in your YouTube live chat. Title is the poll question; Choices is a comma-separated list of up to 4 options.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_endpoll: Ends the currently active YouTube poll. Takes no inputs — Streamer.bot closes whichever poll is open.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_firstwords: Fires the first time a viewer speaks in YouTube Live chat during this stream. User is the newcomer; Message is their first line.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_getuser: Looks up a YouTube user via Streamer.bot. Outputs Id, DisplayName and ProfileImage plus the IsMod / IsSub (member) / IsBroadcaster (channel owner) role flags; Username defaults to the event's user.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_giftmember: Fires once for each viewer who receives a gifted YouTube membership. User is the recipient; Gifter is who paid for it; Tier is the gifted level.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_jewelsgift: Fires when a viewer gifts Jewels on YouTube. User is the gifter; Amount is the gifted amount; Payload carries the raw event JSON. Requires Streamer.bot 1.0.5 or newer.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_membermile: Fires when a member celebrates a membership milestone in YouTube Live chat. Level is the membership level; Months is the total months celebrated; Message is the optional milestone text they shared.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_membership: Fires when a viewer gifts channel memberships on YouTube. User is the gifter; Count is how many memberships were gifted; Tier is the gifted level. Each recipient also raises their own YouTube.GiftMembershipReceived event.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_newsponsor: Fires when a viewer becomes a channel member on YouTube. User is the new member; Level is the membership level name; IsUpgrade is true when an existing member upgraded to a higher level.
Fires when members-only chat is turned off for the YouTube broadcast. Payload carries the raw event JSON.
Fires when members-only chat is turned on for the YouTube broadcast. Payload carries the raw event JSON.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_newsubscri: Fires when someone subscribes to the YouTube channel. User is the new subscriber; Payload carries the raw event JSON for anything beyond that.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_pollclosed: Fires when the YouTube poll closes. Title is the poll question; Payload carries the raw poll JSON with the final results.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_pollstarte: Fires when a poll opens in YouTube Live chat. Title is the poll question; Payload carries the raw poll JSON (option details ride in there).
architect.node.bubble.youtube_pollupdate: Fires when the running YouTube poll updates (fresh votes). Title is the poll question; Payload carries the raw poll JSON with the current tallies.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_presentvie: Fires when Streamer.bot reports the current YouTube viewer list. Users is the list of present viewers, ready for Flow.ForEach or any Array.* node; IsLive says whether the broadcast is currently live.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_sendchat: Sends a chat message into your YouTube live chat as the account connected in Streamer.bot. YouTube caps messages at 200 characters — longer messages are dropped with a log entry instead of being sent truncated.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_setdescrip: Updates the running YouTube broadcast's description. An empty Description is skipped.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_settitle: Updates the running YouTube broadcast's title. An empty Title is skipped.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_seventvemo: Fires when a 7TV emote is added to the channel's YouTube emote set. EmoteName is the emote; Payload carries the raw event JSON.
Fires when a 7TV emote is removed from the channel's YouTube emote set. EmoteName is the emote; Payload carries the raw event JSON.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_statistics: Fires when YouTube refreshes the broadcast statistics. Viewers is the current concurrent-viewer count; Views is the total view count; Likes is the like count.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_superchat: Fires when a viewer sends a SuperChat in YouTube Live chat. User is the sender; Message is the attached text; Amount and Currency carry the purchase value (e.g. 5.00 and "USD"); Tier is YouTube's internal amount tier.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_superstick: Fires when a viewer sends a SuperSticker in YouTube Live chat. Amount and Currency carry the purchase value; StickerAlt is the sticker's alt text; StickerUrl is its image URL.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_timeout: Times User out of your YouTube live chat for Sec seconds. Sec defaults to 300; values below 1 are rejected.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_userbanned: Fires when a user is banned from YouTube Live chat. User is who got banned; BanType distinguishes permanent from temporary bans; Duration is the length in seconds for temporary ones.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_usertimedo: Fires when a user is timed out in YouTube Live chat. User is who got timed out; Duration is the timeout length in seconds. Requires Streamer.bot 1.0.5 or newer.
visualist.canvas.status.audioRequired: The Audio.Play sink cannot be deleted from the canvas — remove the upstream wire instead if you want no audio.
visualist.canvas.status.displayRequired: The Display sink is required and cannot be deleted.
visualist.node.bubble.audio_load: Loads an audio clip from disk for playback. Wire its Audio output into an Audio.Play sink — audio is not drawable, so wiring it into Display does nothing. Path can also be WIRED as a String input, with the attribute as the fallback — that is how ONE Audio.Load plus ONE Audio.Play cover a different clip per alert kind. The clip is latched when the trigger fires: changing the path while it plays does not restart or replace it.
visualist.node.bubble.audio_play: Plays the wired Audio input through the OBS browser source. Volume is 0..1 (full by default); enable Loop for music/ambience, leave it off for one-shot SFX.
visualist.node.bubble.caption_livecaptio: WARNING: the LiveCaption feed is single-stream — only one Caption.LiveCaption widget per layer will receive captions at a time. Multiple Caption.LiveCaption widgets in the same layer will conflict. Outputs the original transcript and a Translated string (equal to the original when TargetLang is empty). PreviewText drives the design-time placeholder so the canvas thumbnail isn't blank.
visualist.node.bubble.color_constant: Outputs a fixed color value (hex string like "#ff8800"). Feed it into Text.Render or anywhere a Color socket is required.
visualist.node.bubble.display: The terminal sink — whatever Image you wire into it gets drawn into the widget's rect in OBS. Auto-injected into every widget graph; the canvas walks upstream from here at evaluation time.
visualist.node.bubble.goal_progress: Reads one goal off the Overlay Live Channel and gives you the pins a progress bar and its caption need: Progress (0..1, clamped), Current, Target, Label, a formatted Text line, and State. Kind selects the goal — follower, sub, bits, tip or charity, or your own custom_ name such as custom_subathon or custom_boss. It is a free-text box on purpose: a dropdown could not express a custom goal. A custom_ kind is used EXACTLY as typed — only the five reserved kinds (follower, sub, bits, tip, charity) are lower-cased for you — so custom_BossHP reads goal.custom_BossHP.* and whatever publishes it must spell it the same way. An unrecognised Twitch goal type is the one exception, and it works the other way round: it arrives as custom_ plus the type in lower case — custom_bit_count, never custom_Bit_Count — so type that Kind in lower case or it will not match. Whatever publishes into it must use these exact keys, shown here for the follower goal: goal.follower.current, goal.follower.target, goal.follower.progress and goal.follower.label (swap follower for the kind you chose). A publisher that fills only current and target still works — Progress is derived from them when no progress was published, and a published progress always wins. A target of 0 or below reads as progress 0, never as finished. PreviewText is design-time only: on stream a goal nobody has published renders nothing rather than placeholder numbers.
visualist.node.bubble.list_live: Binds one literal Overlay Live Channel key whose value is a JSON array and exposes the rows four ways: Text joins the top Size rows through Format, Row gives the single row at Index, Value gives one FIELD of that row raw (wire it into an Image.Load Path for an emote wall or a sponsor logo), and Number gives that field as a number. Count is how many rows arrived; State reports Active, Stale or Empty, and Empty covers both a list nobody published and one that arrived with no rows, so a widget can branch on it to hide itself. TWO VALUE SHAPES ARE ACCEPTED: a real JSON array, which is what a Hub tool publishes, or a string holding that array's JSON text, which is what overlay.publish stores because the script publish surface is string-only by design — so a list published from a .phx script binds here exactly like a tool's. Anything else reads as no rows, and a single object is never promoted to a one-row list. THE FORMAT RULE, which nothing else in the palette follows: the tokens are FIELD NAMES of whatever row shape the publisher chose, not a fixed vocabulary. {index} is the 1-based position and {value} is the row itself when the array holds plain strings; every other {token} is looked up as a field of the row object, case-insensitively, and an unknown one renders empty instead of leaking its braces. A field that arrives as a JSON number is thousands-grouped; a field that arrives as text renders exactly as published, so an all-digit name or a 5.00 amount is never rewritten. So rows shaped name + amount format with {name} and {amount}, and rows shaped label + votes with {label} and {votes}. Index is a wirable input and 1-based: drive it from a Time.Sawtooth and this node becomes a ticker or a sponsor rotator. Out of range yields nothing rather than wrapping back to row 1. PreviewText is design-time only, one mock row per line.
visualist.node.bubble.weboverlay_custom: Renders your own HTML + CSS live over this widget as a DOM overlay above the canvas, so CSS animations, gradients, web fonts and filters work. The 8 String inputs are injected as named CSS variables (--slot1..--slot8, renameable) that an Architect script can drive at runtime via Visual.Trigger. One WebOverlay.Custom per trigger; it renders nothing into the image pipeline, so it cannot be Blend/Mask-composited with canvas image nodes.
visualist.node.bubble.player_embed: Mounts a video player over this whole widget as a real page element above the canvas. Source picks the feed: songrequest follows the Song Request queue Phoenix publishes and reports back when a track ends so the queue advances; clip plays one Twitch clip from the Clip input, wired from a Visual.Arg for a shoutout. The player owns the entire widget rect and cannot be faded, masked or layered against canvas nodes. Playback happens in OBS only, never in the editor preview.
visualist.node.bubble.image_blend: Composites image B (top) over image A (bottom) using a standard CSS blend mode (multiply, screen, overlay, etc.). Opacity (0..1) controls how strongly B shows through. Both A and B are required. Pipeline slot: LAST visual op before Display.
visualist.node.bubble.image_coloradjust: Per-source colour grading: Hue (degrees), Saturation, Brightness, and Contrast (each -1..1, 0 = no change; -1 saturation = greyscale). Pipeline slot: AFTER Crop, BEFORE Transform — so rotation/scale don't bake into colour samples.
visualist.node.bubble.image_combine: Like Image.Blend but adds three key modes that derive alpha from B's pixel values: alpha-key (B's existing alpha), luminance-key (black → transparent), inv-luminance (white → transparent). Convenient when chaining shape generators (Mask.Rectangle, Mask.Circle, etc.) without juggling separate Blend + Mask nodes.
visualist.node.bubble.image_crop: Clips the input image to the rectangle Rect (Vector4: X, Y, W, H, in source-image pixels). Wire from a Vector.Rect4 / Vector4.Constant for clarity. Pipeline slot: FIRST after Load.
visualist.node.bubble.image_load: Loads an image from disk so it can be drawn onto the layer. Set Path to a file under the data/media folder. First step of the canonical pipeline (Load → Crop → ColorAdjust → Transform → Tile → Mask → Blend → Display). Path can also be WIRED as a String input, with the attribute as the fallback, so a graph can choose the file at trigger time (Visual.Arg to String.Select to Path).
visualist.node.bubble.image_loadurl: Loads an image from a remote URL through the Hub asset proxy. Use for live thumbnails, avatars, or anything served over HTTP. Output is an Image you can chain into Crop, Transform, ColorAdjust, etc.
visualist.node.bubble.image_mask: Cuts the Image input through a Mask input — pixels where the mask is opaque (or bright, in luminance mode) survive; the rest go transparent. Both inputs are required. Mode = "alpha" (default) reads the mask's alpha channel; "luminance" uses brightness instead. Pipeline slot: AFTER ColorAdjust / Transform, BEFORE Blend.
visualist.node.bubble.image_scale: Scales the input image by Factor (1 = identity, <1 shrinks, >1 enlarges). Factor can be wired from a Scalar source or set inline. Often the easiest way to grow/shrink a logo without touching Transform.
visualist.node.bubble.image_solid: Fills a rectangle with a Colour and outputs it as an Image — the colour plate the rest of the palette was missing (the Mask.* shapes only ever emit white, and ColorAdjust grades an image rather than painting one). X, Y, Width and Height are 0..1 fractions OF THIS WIDGET FRAME, not of the layer: Width 0.6 means 60% of your own widget, so a bar and its caption compose. That is the one difference from the Mask.* nodes, whose fractions are of the whole layer. All four are WIRABLE inputs, and that is the reason this node exists — wire the Progress pin of Goal.Progress into Width and you have a goal bar with no further nodes. CornerRadius is a fraction of the shorter frame side and stays inline (a pill shape is set once, never driven from data). A rectangle that runs past the frame is not clipped here; Display performs the single crop.
visualist.node.bubble.image_tile: Tiles the input image across the widget rect, repeating Repeat.X times horizontally and Repeat.Y times vertically. Output dimensions match the widget's bounds (the tile fills the widget). Pipeline slot: AFTER Transform, BEFORE Mask / Blend.
visualist.node.bubble.image_transform: Translates, rotates, and scales the input image. Translate is a Vector2 in pixels; Rotate is degrees; Scale is a per-axis Vector2 multiplier. Pipeline slot: AFTER Crop / ColorAdjust, BEFORE Tile / Mask / Blend.
visualist.node.bubble.mask_bezier: Generates a curved polygon mask from a list of bezier vertices (each carrying two control points). Edit via the ShapeEditor modal — there's no inline pill. Use for organic shapes the polygon mask can't hit.
visualist.node.bubble.mask_circle: Generates a circular mask centred at (CX, CY) with the given Radius — all in normalised 0..1 layer space. Feather softens the edge; Inverted swaps inside/outside. Output is an Image.
visualist.node.bubble.mask_ellipse: Generates an ellipse mask with independent RadiusX / RadiusY and an optional Rotation (degrees). All coordinates are normalised 0..1 of the layer. Output is an Image.
visualist.node.bubble.mask_lineargradien: Generates a linear alpha gradient from (FromX, FromY) at FromAlpha to (ToX, ToY) at ToAlpha. All coordinates are normalised 0..1 of the layer. Use as a soft mask for fades and reveals.
visualist.node.bubble.mask_polygon: Generates a straight-edged polygon mask from a list of vertices (normalised 0..1 layer space). Edit the Vertices list via the ShapeEditor modal — there's no inline pill. Closed = true joins the last vertex back to the first.
visualist.node.bubble.mask_radialgradien: Generates a radial alpha gradient centred at (CX, CY), going from InnerAlpha at InnerRadius out to OuterAlpha at OuterRadius. All radii / coords are normalised 0..1 of the layer. Useful for spotlights and soft vignettes.
visualist.node.bubble.mask_rectangle: Generates a rectangle mask (Image output). All coordinates are normalised 0..1 of the layer. CornerRadius rounds the corners; Feather softens the edge; Inverted flips opaque/transparent. Wire into Image.Mask's Mask socket or into Image.Combine.
visualist.node.bubble.mask_star: Generates a star-shaped mask with Points tips (3..16) alternating between OuterRadius and InnerRadius. Rotation, Feather and Inverted work like the other Mask shapes. All coords are normalised 0..1 of the layer.
visualist.node.bubble.mask_vignette: One-knob preset for the classic vignette look — internally renders a Mask.RadialGradient with canonical defaults driven by Strength (0..1, higher = darker corners). Compose with Image.Blend in multiply mode over your image.
visualist.node.bubble.math_add: Adds two scalars: Out = A + B.
visualist.node.bubble.math_clamp: Clamps V to the range [Min, Max]. Use this when an upstream Math chain can drift outside 0..1 before feeding an Opacity / Brightness socket.
visualist.node.bubble.math_div: Divides two scalars: Out = A ÷ B. Returns 0 when B is 0 instead of erroring.
visualist.node.bubble.math_lerp: Linear interpolation between A and B by T (0 = A, 1 = B). T is conventionally 0..1; values outside the band extrapolate.
visualist.node.bubble.math_lerpvector2: Per-component linear interpolation between two Vector2 values by scalar T (0 = A, 1 = B). T is conventionally 0..1.
visualist.node.bubble.math_lerpvector3: Per-component linear interpolation between two Vector3 values by scalar T (0 = A, 1 = B). T is conventionally 0..1.
visualist.node.bubble.math_lerpvector4: Per-component linear interpolation between two Vector4 values by scalar T (0 = A, 1 = B). T is conventionally 0..1.
visualist.node.bubble.math_mul: Multiplies two scalars: Out = A × B. Handy for opacity attenuation (e.g. fade × pulse).
visualist.node.bubble.math_resolution: Outputs the active layer's resolution as a Vector2 (Width, Height). Use it to scale or position widgets relative to the layer size.
visualist.node.bubble.math_sub: Subtracts two scalars: Out = A − B.
visualist.node.bubble.result_if: Branch gate between an Image source and Display. Compares eventData[When] (e.g. "Args1") against Equals; on match, In passes through to Out — on mismatch (or if the named arg is missing) the branch is blocked and emits no image. Compose multiple Result.If nodes in parallel for mutually-exclusive routes (e.g. gamble outcome → win/loss/draw image).
visualist.node.bubble.scalar_constant: Outputs a fixed scalar number, normalised 0..1 by convention (1 = full, 0 = none). Use as an Opacity, Factor, Brightness, etc. driver. Values outside 0..1 are accepted; downstream kernels decide whether to clamp.
visualist.node.bubble.string_select: Maps one string onto another: the first Case row that EXACTLY equals When wins and the node emits that row's Value; when nothing matches, the Default row is emitted. Read this before wiring it: When is the VALUE being matched, NOT an event-data key — wire a Visual.Arg into it. (Result.If has an identically named When attribute and that one IS a key; this one is not.) Matching is exact and case-sensitive, and a Case box left blank counts as an unused row that can never match, so an empty When falls through to Default. Always fill Default in: it is what renders when a value you did not map arrives, which is exactly what happens for an alert kind the Alerts tool labels generically. Twelve rows are available. This is how one Audio.Load or one Image.Load covers a different clip per alert kind instead of one branch per kind.
visualist.node.bubble.text_render: Rasterises a string into an Image so text can flow through the standard Image pipeline (Mask, Blend, Display). Set FontSize, FontFamily, Color, and Alignment (left / center / right). Output is Image.
visualist.node.bubble.text_translate: Translates Text into TargetLang via the Hub-routed translation service. Results are cached per (text, targetLang) so repeated frames don't refire round-trips.
visualist.node.bubble.var_live: Binds one literal key from the Overlay Live Channel — the coalesced 1 Hz key/value stream Hub pushes to this layer. Text gives the value as a string, Number reads it as a number (0 when it is not numeric, never NaN), and State reports how live the key is, so a key nobody has published renders nothing instead of fake placeholder data. State is Active or Missing for nearly every key; the third verdict, Stale, is only reachable when the bound key is a timer.* key, because the Timer tool is the only publisher that declares a refresh cadence for Hub to notice going missing. An event-driven key — counter.*, loyalty.*, caption.*, or one your own script publishes with overlay.publish — is Active from its first publish onward and never decays, so a branch on Stale would never fire for it. Tool keys look like timer.main.progress, counter.deaths.count or loyalty.currency; a script publishes its own with overlay.publish. The Key must be LITERAL: the subscription is read out of this box when the graph loads, so a key built from variables can be published but never bound. PreviewText is design-time only and is never shown on stream. One naming asymmetry worth knowing: on Counter.Value and Loyalty.Balance the State pin carries this same liveness verdict, and on Loyalty.Leaderboard it reports Empty for a board with no rows (that is the word widgets branch on to hide their frame), but on the timer nodes (Timer.Remaining, Countdown.Remaining, Stopwatch.Elapsed) State is the run state of the timer — Running, Paused, Stopped or Ended — and their separate Live pin is what carries Active / Stale / Missing. Caption.LiveCaption has no State pin at all; it exposes Text and Translated only.
visualist.node.bubble.vector2_constant: Outputs a fixed 2-component vector (X, Y). Useful for Image.Transform Translate/Scale or any Vector2 input.
visualist.node.bubble.vector3_combine: Packs three scalars X, Y, Z into a single Vector3 value.
visualist.node.bubble.vector3_constant: Outputs a fixed 3-component vector (X, Y, Z). Pairs with Math.LerpVector3 and the Vector3.Split / Combine nodes.
visualist.node.bubble.vector3_split: Splits a Vector3 into its X, Y, Z scalar components.
visualist.node.bubble.vector4_combine: Packs four scalars X, Y, Z, W into a single Vector4 value.
visualist.node.bubble.vector4_constant: Outputs a fixed 4-component vector (X, Y, Z, W). Use Vector.Rect4 if you want X/Y/W/H labels for crop rectangles instead.
visualist.node.bubble.vector4_split: Splits a Vector4 into its X, Y, Z, W scalar components.
visualist.node.bubble.vector_combine: Packs two scalars X and Y into a single Vector2 value.
visualist.node.bubble.vector_rect4: Friendly alias for a Vector4 with X/Y/W/H labels. Wire its Rect output into Image.Crop or anywhere a rectangle is expected.
visualist.node.bubble.vector_split: Splits a Vector2 into its X and Y scalar components.
visualist.node.bubble.video_load: Plays a local video file as an animated Image source. Set Path to a file under data/media. Defaults to muted + looped so OBS browser-source autoplay works without user interaction. Outputs Image (the current frame) and Duration in seconds. Path can also be WIRED as a String input, with the attribute as the fallback; a dynamically chosen clip is still contain-fitted to the widget rect.
visualist.node.bubble.viewer: Passthrough debug node — drop it on any wire and the value flows through unchanged so the chain keeps working. It previews the incoming image live on the node body; when nothing is wired in yet, it shows an empty card with a hint instead.
visualist.node.bubble.visual_arg: Reads one named field out of the trigger payload Hub sent and outputs it as a String. Key is the field name: a script Visual.Trigger with Args set to a,b,c arrives as Args1, Args2 and Args3; the Alerts tool puts the alert kind in Args1, the viewer name in Args2 and the size (bits, months, raiders) in Args3; chat-fed triggers also carry user and message. PreviewText is a DESIGN-TIME placeholder only — on stream a field that was never supplied renders nothing, never the placeholder. That is the one difference from the older Message.Read node, whose MockValue does show on stream; prefer this node in new graphs. Wire it into String.Select to pick a clip or an image per kind, or into Text.Render to show the value.
visualist.node.bubble.visual_complete: Lifecycle sink — when graph evaluation reaches this node, the compositor signals VISUAL_COMPLETE back to Hub so any wait_for_visual script proceeds on its Done branch. If a graph has no Visual.Complete, the engine falls back to firing on the first Display render. TWO SEPARATE INPUTS: In is the ordering pin, kept for symmetry with Display — nothing wired into it is ever rendered. Payload is the new one: wire a String and its value travels up with the completion into the script's global._wait_payload, readable on Async.WaitForVisual's Payload output. Leave Payload unwired and the field is omitted entirely, exactly as before. FAN-OUT WARNING: every widget that owns the fired trigger on this layer shares ONE waitId, and the FIRST completion to arrive wins — later ones are dropped and logged once. So with two OBS Browser Sources pointed at the same layer, WHICH widget's Payload reaches the script is not predictable; use one source per layer when the payload has to be deterministic.
visualist.node.bubble.visual_onstartup: Fires once when the layer activates in OBS. Outputs the LayerId (string) and a Timestamp (seconds). Use it to seed widgets that should render immediately on layer load.
visualist.node.bubble.visual_ontrigger: Entry point for a widget trigger. Outputs the trigger context that arrived from Hub: TriggerName, EventData (raw JSON), UserName, and Message. The Name attribute selects which named trigger this node listens for (e.g. "onTrigger:hype").

dialog.settings.diagnostics.freeze_intro: If the interface ever freezes, Phoenix already saves a small diagnostic snapshot automatically. A full snapshot additionally captures the app's whole memory, which is what makes some freezes identifiable at all. Leave this off unless you are actively investigating one.
dialog.settings.diagnostics.full_memory_: Capture a full memory snapshot when the interface freezes

Two things to know: the freeze lasts longer, because the automatic restart waits for the snapshot to finish writing (up to 2 minutes) instead of restarting after 12 seconds — avoid this while live. And the file contains everything the app held in memory at that moment, including connection details and chat, so treat it as private.
